answers.text: Yes. With a 10-minute hold and a webhook up to 30 minutes late, a lapsed hold is an expected case, and the refund path handles it. The 10 minutes is a fixed requirement in the brief; I do not know the reason for that number and have not invented one. Noted in Open questions and in failure branch 3.

Order retries the call a few times with the same order id (safe because Inventory and Payment treat a repeat as the same request). If still no answer, the order becomes CHECKOUT_FAILED, publishes OrderFailed so any hold is released, and the customer is told to try again; the cart is untouched. A charge that did reach the provider and later succeeds is turned into a refund because the order is already failed. Chosen as the simplest handling; added as status CHECKOUT_FAILED and failure branch 6.

Payment stores the payment as PENDING and answers 202 accepted at once; the real outcome only comes by webhook. Order sets AWAITING_PAYMENT before it makes the charge call, so a failed call still leaves a known status. Added to the AWAITING_PAYMENT box.

Order learns the claim result from the HTTP reply of the claim call (accepted or refused); I made the arrows say so. The arrow from the timer into the refuse box was wrong and is removed. The timer only marks holds EXPIRED; the claim itself refuses by reading status EXPIRED, or HELD but past expires_at.

Nothing stopped it before. Now Order allows one open order (PENDING or AWAITING_PAYMENT) per cart id, with a unique rule, and a second press returns the open order. So one reservation and one charge per cart. Cart id is sent in the snapshot. Added as failure branch 7.

The snapshot and the OrderConfirmed event carry the cart id, and Cart empties that cart. The polling page shows: CONFIRMED order placed; PAYMENT_FAILED payment declined, try again; CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK out of stock, full refund on the way; also REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK shows short items and CHECKOUT_FAILED says try again. Added a table.

Usually the timer has already made it EXPIRED, but it may still be HELD past expires_at if the timer has not run. Nothing released it before. Now Order also publishes OrderFailed on the cancel path, and release does nothing if the hold is already expired or released, so it is safe either way.

Payment runs both jobs inside its own service, scanning its own tables. The retry job finds refunds with status REQUESTED or RETRYING whose next attempt time is due. The stuck state is now named RETRYING. The silent-provider check is a Payment timer that scans PENDING payments older than 35 minutes and asks the provider for the status by order id; I moved it into the diagram and trigger table. The 35-minute figure is my assumption, not from the brief.

questions.text: When Order receives PaymentSucceeded, how does it decide between asking for the claim (O7) and asking for a refund? Which statuses lead to which, and where is that shown in the flowchart?

questions.text: What does the provider answer to the 35-minute status check if the charge is still undecided? Does Payment keep asking, and what does the customer see while the order waits in AWAITING_PAYMENT?

questions.text: How does a webhook get matched to a payment and order? Does the webhook carry the order id or the provider reference?
If PaymentDeclined arrives for an order that is already CHECKOUT_FAILED (or any final status), what does Order do? What does 'only moves an order forward from the status it expects' mean in practice?
What is the relay and what runs it? If it is down or slow, which steps stall and what does the customer see?

answers.text: Order reads its own status when PaymentSucceeded arrives. If it is still AWAITING_PAYMENT, it asks Inventory to claim. If the order already failed (for example CHECKOUT_FAILED), it makes no claim and publishes RefundRequested. If it is CONFIRMED or CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the event is a repeat and is ignored. Chosen because money must never be kept for an order that cannot be fulfilled. This was missing from the flowchart; I added a diamond and a refund box.

If the provider says the charge is still undecided, Payment leaves it PENDING and the same timer asks again on its next run, so it keeps asking. The customer sees Processing the whole time, since the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT. Whether to stop or alert a person after some time is not decided; I added it to Open questions. Added to the timer box, the polling table and failure branch 8.

Payment stores the provider reference when it makes the charge, and the webhook is matched by that reference, which gives the order id. I have not verified what a real provider's webhook carries, so this is an assumption, listed under Assumptions. If the provider can echo the order id, that works as well.

Order ignores it: PaymentDeclined for an order already CHECKOUT_FAILED or any final status does nothing, and the hold was already released by OrderFailed. 'Only moves forward from the status it expects' means each handler updates the order only if the status is the expected one (AWAITING_PAYMENT for PaymentDeclined and PaymentSucceeded), otherwise it does nothing. The one exception is PaymentSucceeded on a failed order, which triggers a refund. Added as failure branch 9 and in the design rules.

The relay is a small background loop inside each service that reads unsent rows from that service's own outbox table, publishes them to the broker and marks them sent. If it is down or slow, events wait in the outbox and nothing is lost. Steps that depend on the event stall, and the customer keeps seeing Processing until it is published. Which process hosts it is not otherwise specified. Added to the design rules, stores section and failure branch 10.

questions.text: After Payment has answered 202, what happens if the provider never accepts the charge request after its retries? How would that order ever leave AWAITING_PAYMENT, and what does the customer see?
questions.about: Payment answers 202 accepted at once / retry with the same key if the provider does not answer

answers.text: Order retries the claim a few times with the same order id (claim is idempotent per order id). If there is still no answer, the order becomes CHECKOUT_FAILED and Order publishes RefundRequested and OrderFailed. The money is already taken, so the order must not wait forever; refunding is the simplest rule that never keeps money for an order we cannot confirm. The cost is that a claim which did succeed in Inventory is refunded anyway. Added a box, edges and failure branch 6.

The stored record comes first. Payment stores the payment as PENDING with the order id, then calls the provider with the order id as idempotency key. The provider's reply supplies the provider reference, which Payment then stores on the payment. The box was wrong before. The 35-minute check looks the charge up by order id, so a crash between the reply and the store is still recoverable. A webhook arriving before the reference is stored is not decided; added to Open questions.

After retries with the same key, if the provider never accepts, Payment stores DECLINED and publishes PaymentDeclined, so Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED, releases the hold and the customer is told. This reuses the existing declined path instead of adding a mechanism. If that charge did reach the provider and succeeds later, Payment stores SUCCEEDED over DECLINED and publishes PaymentSucceeded; Order sees the order is not AWAITING_PAYMENT and requests a refund. Added an edge and a line in branch 6.

teachbacks.text:
Walkthrough of one order from Place order to the end, following the main (success) path and noting the failure branches as they come up.

1. **Customer presses Place order.** Cart starts this. It takes a snapshot of the cart lines and prices as they are at that moment and sends it, with the cart id, to Order over HTTP. Cart holds the live cart and is not changed. If this step fails, nothing exists yet and the customer just presses the button again.

2. **Order creates the order.** Order stores a row with status `PENDING`, holding the snapshot, the total and the cart id. This fixes the order id. Order's database has a unique rule of one open order (`PENDING` or `AWAITING_PAYMENT`) per cart id. A second press or double click returns the existing open order, so there is only one hold and one charge per cart.

3. **Order asks Inventory to reserve.** Order calls Inventory over HTTP, sending the order id and lines. Inventory reserves every line in one database transaction, or none. It sets `expires_at` 10 minutes ahead and records the reservation as `HELD` in its own database. A repeat call with the same order id counts as the same reservation. Order retries a few times if there is no answer.
   - Short stock: Inventory reserves nothing and returns the short items. Order sets `REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK`, shows the customer the short items and never calls Payment. The cart is unchanged.
   - No answer after retries: Order sets `CHECKOUT_FAILED`, tells the customer to retry, and publishes `OrderFailed`, which makes Inventory release the hold. The cart is unchanged.

4. **Order asks Payment to charge.** Order first sets `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, so a failed call still leaves a known status. It then calls Payment over HTTP to charge the snapshot total. Payment stores a payment row `PENDING` with the order id, answers 202 accepted at once, and asks the provider to charge, using the order id as the idempotency key. The provider's reply gives a provider reference, which Payment stores on the payment. The customer sees Processing and the page polls the order status. A repeat charge call for the same order is treated as the same payment. If Payment does not answer Order after retries, Order sets `CHECKOUT_FAILED` and publishes `OrderFailed`.

5. **If the provider never accepts the charge.** Order already has its 202, so Payment handles this itself. It retries with the same key. If the provider still never accepts, Payment stores `DECLINED` and publishes `PaymentDeclined`, which continues at step 9.

6. **Waiting for the provider.** The provider reports the outcome later by webhook to Payment, seconds to 30 minutes after the charge. The order stays `AWAITING_PAYMENT` and the customer sees Processing. If no webhook comes about 35 minutes after the charge, a Payment timer asks the provider for the status by order id. If the answer is still undecided, the payment stays `PENDING` and the timer asks again on its next run. A definite answer is handled like a webhook.

7. **Webhook arrives.** Payment finds the payment by provider reference. In one transaction it inserts the provider's event id (unique constraint) and stores the outcome. If the insert fails, the webhook is a duplicate, so Payment replies 200 and does nothing. Otherwise it publishes `PaymentSucceeded` or `PaymentDeclined`. Every event is written to the service's outbox table in the same transaction as the state change. A relay loop then publishes unsent rows to the broker. Delivery is at least once, so every consumer must tolerate repeats.

8. **Order handles PaymentSucceeded.** Order reads its own status in its own database.
   - `AWAITING_PAYMENT`: go to step 10 to claim.
   - Already failed, for example `CHECKOUT_FAILED`: no claim, status unchanged, and Order publishes `RefundRequested`. This also covers a payment Payment had stored as `DECLINED`, which it then overwrites with `SUCCEEDED`.
   - `CONFIRMED` or `CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK`: a repeat, so do nothing.

9. **Declined path.** On `PaymentDeclined`, if the order is `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, Order sets `PAYMENT_FAILED`, tells the customer, and publishes `OrderFailed`. Inventory consumes `OrderFailed` and releases the hold, which is safe to repeat. The cart is unchanged. If the customer presses Place order again, that makes a new order id and so a new idempotency key. A `PaymentDeclined` for an order in any other status is ignored.

10. **Order asks Inventory to claim.** Order calls Inventory over HTTP with the same order id. In one transaction Inventory checks that the hold is `HELD` and not past `expires_at`. The claim checks the time itself and does not rely on the expiry timer.
    - Yes: the hold becomes `CLAIMED` (the stock is sold) and Inventory replies accepted. Order sets `CONFIRMED` and publishes `OrderConfirmed` with the cart id (step 12).
    - No (the hold is `EXPIRED`, or still `HELD` but past `expires_at`): Inventory replies refused. Go to step 11.
    - No answer after retries: money is already taken, so Order sets `CHECKOUT_FAILED`, publishes `RefundRequested` and `OrderFailed`, and tells the customer to try again with a refund on the way. The document says this refunds even if Inventory did claim the stock.

11. **Late success.** A lapsed hold is expected, because the hold lasts 10 minutes but the provider can take up to 30. On a refused claim Order sets `CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK`, publishes `RefundRequested` and `OrderFailed`, and emails the customer that the item is out of stock and a full refund is on the way. The release does nothing if the hold is already expired. The cart is unchanged.

12. **Cart empties.** Cart consumes `OrderConfirmed` and empties the cart named in it. This is the only place the cart is ever emptied.

13. **Refund (on any RefundRequested).** Payment writes one refund record `REQUESTED` per order id, so a repeat is a no-op, before it calls the provider. It then asks the provider to refund the full amount, with the order id as key. If the provider confirms, the record becomes `REFUNDED` and Payment publishes `RefundCompleted`. Order records that and emails the customer that the refund is issued. If the call fails or times out, the record becomes `RETRYING` with the attempt count and last error. Payment's retry job rescans its own refunds that are `REQUESTED` or `RETRYING` and due, and re-runs them with backoff. It never gives up, and after N failures it also alerts a person.

14. **Release.** Inventory releases a hold on `OrderFailed`. Separately, a timer runs every minute and marks `HELD` holds older than 10 minutes as `EXPIRED`, putting the stock back on sale. The timer refuses nothing.

15. **Event relay down.** Events wait in the outbox and nothing is lost. Steps that need them wait, and the customer keeps seeing Processing.
gaps: How the customer's Place order press reaches Cart and how Cart knows which cart (the document does not describe the front-end or Cart's entry point, only that Cart sends the snapshot to Order)
What Payment does with a webhook that arrives before it has stored the provider reference (the document lists this as an open question), so I cannot say how the webhook is matched in that case
How many times Order retries the reserve, charge and claim calls, and the value of N before a person is alerted (the document says these are not decided)
What the page does or shows once the order reaches a final status other than the table entries, and how the page polling reaches Order (the document does not say whether the page asks Order directly)

Whether the broker routes events to specific consumers (for example which service listens to which event type) and how consumers subscribe. The flowchart shows who handles each event, but the document does not say how routing works.

What the customer-facing result is when Inventory's reserve call gets no answer but a hold may actually have been made. The document does not say how that hold is released other than via OrderFailed, which it does mention for this case, but it does not say what happens if the reserve did succeed and the reply was lost beyond that.
